item.title: Rigid continua containing an arbitrary Peano continuum
item.description: arXiv:2611.09480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bani\v c and Kac, and later \v Crepnjak and Kac, constructed an uncountable family of continua with different types of rigidity. For every continuum $X$ with the mentioned property, the inverse limit $\varprojlim\{X,f_n\}$ is homeomorphic to $X$ for an arbitrary sequence of continuous surjective functions $f_n: X \to X$. We extend these results by proving that for any Peano continuum $X$ there exists an uncountable family ${\cal F}$ of rigid, for each positive integer $m$, $\frac{1}{m}$-rigid, and $0$-rigid continua such that each $Y \in {\cal F}$ contains a homeomorphic copy of $X$ and for each $Y \in {\cal F}$ it holds that the inverse limit $\varprojlim\{Y,f_n\}$ is homeomorphic to $Y$ for arbitrarily sequence of continuous surjective functions $f_n: Y \to Y$.
item.dc:creator: Matev\v{z} \v{C}repnjak (University of Maribor), Teja Kac (University of Maribor), Tina Sovi\v{c} (University of Maribor)

item.title: On two examples of topological gyrogroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.09486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we construct an infinite-dimensional topological gyrogroup that fails to be strongly topological. We equip the countable direct sum of the complex unit disk with a carefully weighted infinite series of component seminorms. By dividing the infinite-dimensional operation into a finite core and a bounded infinite tail, we rigorously prove the joint continuity of the M\"obius addition, confirming the space is a valid topological gyrogroup. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the gyroautomorphisms exhibit unbounded expansion under this real seminorm topology, explicitly preventing the existence of an invariant neighborhood basis at the identity. This provides a clear, analytic counterexample separating general topological gyrogroups from strongly topological ones. Moreover, we construct a topological gyrogroup which is not strongly topological but it contains a non-trivial strong subgyrogroup.
item.dc:creator: Meng Bao, Piyu Li

item.title: A Stone-Weierstrass Theorem for Polish Spaces, Given by Logic
item.description: arXiv:2611.08901v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Stone-Weierstrass theorem obtains every continuous function on a compact space as a uniform limit of functions built from a separating family by finitely many operations, and Reggio proved the theorem equivalent to the Beth definability property of an infinitary equational logic. We extend both results beyond compactness: on every separable metric space, and in particular on every Polish space, every bounded uniformly continuous function is a uniform limit of functions built from countably many bounded separating functions by the connectives of infinitary real-valued logic, and an approximate Beth property of this logic is equivalent to the new theorem. The extension rests on a rule of syntax, which admits a countable supremum when its terms share an a priori bound and thereby makes the sentences define exactly the bounded Lipschitz functions, and on a model existence game that does the work of compactness in the proof of interpolation.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: Joint Approximation and the Mixed-Prime Character Group
item.description: arXiv:2611.08964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the integer metric defined by the square denominators of two distinct primes, we prove simultaneous approximation to zero in one prime metric and to any prescribed integer in the other. A normalized convolution argument gives a uniform central spectral bound. Random relative translations of smooth weights produce an exact positive cas cade; Fourier positivity places every normalized finer convolution below its value at zero. A far-field recursion, the growth of merged square powers, and a two-term logarithmic-form estimate give summable fac tor bounds. Consequently, for every fixed pair of distinct primes p,q, the mixed continuous character group is Z[1/(pq)]/Z: no irrational pa rameter is continuous. The mixed completion is the product of the one-prime completions. For each fixed pair this also gives a compati ble rational join and a strictly finer compatible join of the associated real TVG topologies, with the same prescribed real character group. Exact witness search terminates at every strict precision and integer target. We retain the structural, density, divisibility, sequence and finite-certificate results leading to this proof. The existence argument does not give practical witness-size or runtime bounds, and it does not assume independence or equidistribution of the two digit systems. Se lected abstract components have been checked using Lean and Mathlib; the complete analytic argument has not been formalized. The corre sponding problem for three or more primes remains separate.
item.dc:creator: Irina Yaroshevskaya

item.title: Topological Mundici Adjunction and Its Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.09608v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a canonical topological lifting of Mundici equivalence, representing every topological MV-algebra as the unit interval of a topological $\ell$-group and extending the correspondence to a categorical adjunction. As applications, we give a direct group-theoretic proof of the equivalence of $T_0$ and $T_{3\frac12}$ and show that every topological MV-algebra is a retral space. We further extend the lifting to topological Riesz MV-algebras and identify the canonical topology with Wiweger's mixed topology under suitable assumptions, recovering the strict topology as a special case. Finally, we obtain a unit-interval formulation of Koopman representations for continuous-time dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Yanqiao Jia, Xueting Zhao, Yichuan Yang
